_why: Needles whose anchor matches MORE THAN ONCE inside the scope its own harness
counts in. Such a needle is a mutant that may not run, or may run somewhere
nobody aimed it — the battery's denominator counts it and its power does not.
This is a RATCHET, the same shape as frontend/typecheck-baseline.json: anything
not listed here fails the scan. Fixing one prints a nudge and does not fail,
because blocking a lane for repairing a guard would be perverse.
To clear an entry: make the needle unique (usually by extending it with the
next line that differs), confirm the harness scores the mutant KILLED rather
than HARNESS-FAIL, and delete the line.
THE LIST IS EMPTY, AND FOUR OF THE ORIGINAL SEVEN WERE NEVER DEBT (#2391).
The seven recorded here on 2026-08-31 were graded by a scan that counted every
needle against its whole target file and assumed every harness in this
directory refuses a non-unique anchor. Three of the four harnesses involved do
not, so the scan was reporting its own assumption back as debt:
REAL, now fixed (the anchor was extended until unique):
game_markets_shared_cache_mutations:M14 — matched 3x; the serve-stale
shape is copied verbatim across search_suggestions, game_markets and
related_futures. Measured HARNESS (14/15 killed) before, KILLED after.
search_word_test_mutations:fragment-boundary-always-exempts
search_word_test_mutations:fragment-boundary-back-to-length — matched 2x
each. These DID run: the harness had no uniqueness check and
`replace(..., 1)` took the leftmost match, which happened to be the
intended site. Correct by line ORDER, not by contract. Both anchors are
pinned now and that harness enforces a count, so the accident cannot
recur.
NOT DEBT — the scan was measuring the wrong thing:
search_tier_split_mutations:M6-no-rearm — the harness counts inside
`inspect.getsource(_fetch_futures_window)`, where the anchor appears
once; the second match is in another function it never touches. Verified
KILLED, 8/8, while still 'ambiguous' on the old scan.
outcome_evidence_class_mutations:M1, :M3, :M4 — the target is the
GENERATED search_gold_probes.json, where `"split": "canary"` recurs once
per probe by construction. That harness has always exempted the registry
on purpose and mutates exactly one occurrence.
Both facts are now READ from the harness rather than assumed by the scan:
`anchor_scope_text()` publishes a narrower counting scope, and
`ANCHOR_MAY_REPEAT_IN` publishes a legitimately-repeating target. Each is the
same expression the harness's own check uses, so the two cannot drift into
disagreeing — the `MUTATES_WORKING_TREE` convention, applied to aim.
